name: Non-specific Autoimmune Brainstem Encephalitis with Characteristic Antibodies

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Proposed Criteria for Autoimmune Brainstem Encephalitis

criteria.description: Subacute onset of brainstem neurological symptoms including diplopia, dysarthria, and ataxia
Presence of characteristic autoantibodies targeting neuronal antigens in serum or cerebrospinal fluid
MRI evidence of brainstem inflammation or lesions consistent with encephalitis
Cerebrospinal fluid pleocytosis or elevated protein indicating inflammation
Exclusion of infectious, neoplastic, metabolic, or other autoimmune etiologies

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of subacute brainstem neurological symptoms, detection of characteristic autoantibodies, MRI evidence of brainstem inflammation, and exclusion of other causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis relies heavily on antibody testing and neuroimaging combined with clinical presentation.

pathognomonic.notes: Commonly manifests as diplopia and ptosis

searchTerms: speech problems due to brainstem involvement

pathognomonic.symptomName: Ataxia secondary to cerebellar pathway disruption
searchTerms: balance problems due to brain pathway disruption
trouble eating due to cranial nerve damage
problems with automatic body functions including low blood pressure when standing
autonomic nervous system dysfunction causing dizziness

rare.symptomName: Respiratory failure due to brainstem respiratory center involvement
searchTerms: respiratory arrest due to brain injury

rare.symptomName: Psychiatric symptoms such as anxiety or hallucinations
searchTerms: psychiatric symptoms like fear or seeing things

laboratory: Detection of characteristic neuronal autoantibodies (e.g., anti-Hu, anti-Ma2, anti-Ri) in serum or CSF
CSF pleocytosis and elevated protein concentration
imaging: MRI showing T2/FLAIR hyperintensities localized to the brainstem
other: Electrophysiological studies may show brainstem conduction abnormalities
Exclusion of infectious and neoplastic causes by appropriate testing

distinguishingFeatures: Imaging consistent with ischemia rather than inflammation
Presence of oligoclonal bands in CSF
Fever and systemic signs of infection

redFlags: New onset seizures or altered mental status
references: Lancaster E. The diagnosis and treatment of autoimmune encephalitis. J Clin Neurol. 2016;12(1):1-13.
Graus F, et al. A clinical approach to diagnosis of autoimmune encephalitis. Lancet Neurol. 2016;15(4):391-404.
Dalmau J, Rosenfeld MR. Autoimmune encephalitis update. Neuro Oncol. 2014;16(6):771-778.
